column2: On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): “A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: Advise me. He said: Do not become angry. The man repeated [his request] several times, and he said: Do not become angry.” Reported by al-Bukhārī.
Rajulan (“a man”): it is said he was Abū al-Dardāʾ, and it is said someone else.
Awṣinī (“advise me”): [give me] advice comprising the qualities of goodness.
Lā taghḍab (“do not become angry”): do not expose yourself to anything that brings anger upon you, and do not carry out its effects on others. Fa-raddada: he repeated.
A warning against anger, because it gathers every evil, while guarding against it gathers every good.
The command to adopt virtuous character traits that keep one far from anger, such as forbearance, gentleness and humility.
Patience with what befalls a person in this world, and treating people well.

In this hadith the noble Prophet ﷺ advises us to leave anger, because it is of the nature of the devil, and not to act on its effects, lest great harm come to us because of it, sooner or later. Rather, we should hold back from anger and what it impels us to do, and repel it by adopting forbearance, gentleness

and deliberateness, for in that is much good. Even if no harm came from anger except the change of the colour of the face and violent movement of the limbs—and perhaps the angry person's tongue is let loose with insults and obscene speech, and perhaps he commits an offence against someone by striking or killing, so that his state becomes bad now and later—these punishments would be enough to deter one from these effects and others.
That is why the Prophet ﷺ advised the questioner, repeating to him that he should not become angry.
(A note) Among the means of warding off anger:
1. One should remember the virtue of restraining anger.
2. One should seek refuge with Allah from the accursed devil.
3. One should make wuḍūʾ.
4. One should change one's position: if standing, sit down, and if sitting, lie down.
5. One should remember the anger of Allah, and that His retribution is above that, and so fear Allah.
And other things by which a person treats himself for anger and guards against its evil effects. We seek refuge with Allah from evil anger.
A point of benefit:

It is related that a man's servant brought him food in a dish, but the servant tripped on the carpet and what he was carrying fell, and the man was filled with rage. The servant said: “My master, act on the saying of Allah the Exalted.” The man said: “And what is the saying of Allah the Exalted?”

He said: “Allah the Exalted said: ‘…and who restrain anger…’” The man said: “I have restrained my anger.” The servant said: “‘…and who pardon people…’” He said: “I have pardoned you.” The servant said: “‘…and Allah loves the doers of good’ [Āl ʿImrān 3:134].” The man said: “You are free for the sake of Allah,” and gave him a thousand dinars.
Forbearance is not [shown] in times of contentment; / forbearance is only [shown] in times of anger.
Another poet:
Among the enemies I tested, I never saw / an enemy more hostile to a man's mind than anger.
And in the proverb: “Anger is the seed of regret.”
